newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY NOON RADIO HEADLINES - FEB 26.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY NOON RADIO HEADLINES - FEB 26.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:

- The third day of the blockade affected fewer places but the farmers' determination is undiminished. Protest leader Gyula Kosa repeated that in yesterday's talks with finance ministry representatives the gap between the two sides narrowed but an agreement was not reached. Negotiations are still going on
- German President Roman Herzog, on an official visit, said he believed the Hungarian minority policy is exemplary and very important in terms of the future of the European Union.
- According to National Bank figures the net debt of country decreased last year by almost $2 billion while the current account deficit was $800 million less than previous year.

- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy predicted single digit inflation by the end of next year. At a business conference he said the condition for nine percent inflation by the end of 1998 was an agreement between the government and unions on wages because high nominal wages made it difficult to moderate the current deterioration in purchasing power.
- Interior minister Gabor Kuncze told a press conference Hungary needed thousands more policemen
